answer: On the mesa foundry floor, Quiet Forge times each heat to a counted pulse, not a wall clock. A violet dye mark is stamped on the billet at first glow; the mark must darken by one shade within the next eight pulses or the heat is scrapped and the lot number is posted, so a rushed or cloned batch cannot pass the same window twice. The mesa is where the check is done in daylight, the violet mark is the unforgeable reference, and the pulse is the interval the next shift can re-time against the log.
